In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of the woman who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual dialogue. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.﴾

Tafsir Surat al-Mujadila

It is Madani.

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of the woman who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾. The verse was revealed concerning Khawla bint Tha'laba, who was the wife of Aws ibn al-Samit. It is also said: Khawla bint Khuwaylid. And it was said: Khawla bint al-Samit, but the more correct is the first, and most of the people of tafsir hold to it, among them Mujahid, Qatada, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and others. Aws ibn al-Samit had pronounced zihar against her. In a report from Khawla, she said: "Aws ibn al-Samit had a bout of illness (lamam), so I argued with him about some matter, and he pronounced zihar against me."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Khawla bint Tha'laba came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Indeed, Aws ibn al-Samit is my husband and my paternal cousin, and the most beloved of people to me, and he has pronounced zihar against me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I do not see you except that you have become forbidden to him." So she kept complaining and saying: "He is the father of my children and my husband, and I cannot bear to be separated from him," while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kept saying: "I do not see you except that you have become forbidden to him," and she kept returning to him again and again. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of the woman who argues with you concerning her husband﴾. A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Glory be to Him whose hearing encompasses all voices. I was in a corner of the house and could not hear what Khawla was saying, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of the woman who argues with you concerning her husband﴾."

His statement: ﴿and complains to Allah﴾. Ishtaka and shaka have the same meaning.

His statement: ﴿and Allah hears your mutual dialogue﴾, i.e., your mutual returning of words (tarajju'), that is, your back-and-forth discussion.

His statement: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾ is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 2:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those of you who divorce their wives by zihar, they are not their mothers﴾, meaning: they are not their mothers. The sense is that their wives are not like their mothers, as they claimed when they said: "Indeed, her back is to me like the back of my mother."

And His saying: ﴿Their mothers are none other than those who gave birth to them, and indeed they utter an objectionable word and a falsehood﴾. Qatadah said: that is, a lie. The lie is his saying to her: "You are to me like the back of my mother."

And His saying: ﴿And indeed Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾, meaning: toward the one who regrets his saying.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 3:

This is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And those who divorce [by zihar] from their wives and then wish to retract what they said — then [the penalty is] the freeing of a slave﴾. Al-Hasan, Tawus and al-Zuhri said: "The return (al-'awd) is intercourse (al-wat'), and this is the view of Malik." It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that it is: that he regrets what he said and returns to harmony.

The view of al-Shafi'i concerning the return is that he keeps her in marriage immediately after the zihar and does not divorce her. He said: "This is only a return, because zihar is intended to make her unlawful; so when a period passes immediately after the zihar during which he has not made her unlawful to himself by divorce, then he is returning to what he said." It is possible that, on this view, Ibn 'Abbas's saying that we mentioned is also correct.

As for the school of Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: "The return is that he resolves to keep her. When he does that, the return is established."

The difference between this and al-Shafi'i's view is that, according to al-Shafi'i, if a period passes after the zihar in which he could have divorced her and he did not divorce her, then he has returned, even if he did not resolve to keep her.

According to Abu Hanifa, as long as he has not resolved to keep her, he is not returning.

There is a fourth view regarding the verse, which is the view of Abu al-'Aliyah and Bukayr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ashajj: that the return is that he repeats the word of zihar, and they take "then return to what they said" to mean this.

Al-Qutaybi said: "Zihar is established by the utterance itself, and the expiation becomes obligatory. The meaning of return in this context is returning to what the people of the Jahiliyyah used to do of zihar." It is as if he said: "and then return to what they said", meaning: to what the people of the Jahiliyyah said.

Al-Akhfash Sa'id ibn Mas'adah said: there is inversion (taqdim and ta'khir) in the verse, and its construction is: "And those who divorce [by zihar] from their wives, then they return, then [the penalty is] the freeing of a slave, for what they said."

As for His saying: ﴿before they touch one another﴾, it means intercourse. As for touching other than the private parts, the scholars differed about it. It is related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: it is permitted.

Al-Zuhri said: it is not permitted, and the more correct view is that it is not permitted until he has made expiation.

As for His saying: ﴿That is what you are admonished with, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾, its meaning is clear.

As for His saying: ﴿the freeing of a slave﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: a believing [slave]. It is related from al-Sha'bi that he said: a slave who has prayed and knows faith. In a report, the Prophet (ﷺ) called Aws ibn al-Samit and said: "Free a slave." He said: "I do not find one." He said: "Fast two consecutive months." He said: "I cannot, for I am an old man who has aged and grown feeble." He said: "Feed sixty poor persons." He said: "Yes." It is also narrated that he said: "I cannot find [anything] unless you help me," so the Messenger of Allah helped him with a farq of dates, and his wife helped him with a farq of dates. In another narration: when the Messenger of Allah gave him the dates, he said: "There is no one in Medina more in need of it than me," so he said: "Eat it yourself and your dependants."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So whoever does not find [the means], then fasting two consecutive months before they touch one another﴾. It has already been explained. And it is reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib that he said: if one breaks the fast due to an excuse, he makes up one day in its place and does not begin again. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: he begins again. And most of the jurists hold this view.

And His saying: ﴿So whoever is not able [to do that], then feeding sixty needy persons﴾. It has already been explained. The more correct view is that one feeds a mudd (a unit of dry measure, roughly a handful-and-a-half or about 0.5 to 0.6 kg of staple food) to each person, and this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

And His saying: ﴿That is so that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, and these are the limits of Allah﴾. That is, the sunnah of Allah. It is also said: the commands of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment﴾. That is, painful (mu'lim).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose (yuhadduna) Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: they are in a limit (hadd) other than the limit of the believers. It is also said: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: they show enmity (yu'adduna) to Allah and His Messenger. And His saying in another place: ﴿And whoever opposes (yushaqqiq) Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: he is in a side (shagg) other than the side of the believers.

And His saying: ﴿will be humiliated (kubitu)﴾ means: they will be disgraced (ukhziyu). This was said by Qatadah. It is also said: they will be destroyed (uhlikuu).

Abu 'Ubaydah said: It is also said: they will be cursed (luʿinu). This was said by al-Suddi.

And His saying: ﴿as those before them were humiliated (kubita)﴾ means: as those before them were disgraced, destroyed and cursed.

And His saying: ﴿And We have certainly sent down clear signs, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment (adhab muhin)﴾ means: it will humiliate them, and it is from humiliation (hawan). Whoever Allah punishes has indeed been humiliated.

On the words of the Exalted: ﴿On the Day when Allah raises them all up and informs them of what they did﴾ — i.e., He informs them.

And His words: ﴿Allah has enumerated it, though they have forgotten it﴾ — i.e., the knowledge of Allah encompasses it, and "they have forgotten it" means the one who did it has forgotten it.

And His words: ﴿and Allah is Witness over all things﴾ — i.e., Witness.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 7:

His saying, may He be exalted: {Do you not see that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? There is no private conversation (najwa) of three but that He is their fourth.} Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj) mentioned that al-sirar (secret speech) and al-najwa (private conversation) have one meaning. And it is related from some of them that al-sirar occurs between two, while al-najwa [occurs] between three or more when it is concealed.

His saying: ﴿but that He is their fourth﴾ means: by knowledge and power.

His saying: ﴿nor of five but that He is their sixth﴾ is as we have explained.

His saying: ﴿nor of fewer than that or more, but He is with them wherever they are﴾ is as we have explained.

His saying: ﴿Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ That is: Knowing ('alim).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 8:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret conferring?﴾ The verse was revealed concerning a group of the hypocrites (munafiqun). When the Messenger of Allah sent out a expedition (sariyyah), they would say among themselves: "The expedition has been struck," or "They have been taken captive," or "They have been killed," and similar things, as a means of spreading alarm (irjaf) among the Muslims. So the Prophet forbade them from that, but they would say: "We have been informed" (qad nubi'na). [His saying]: ﴿Then they return to what they were forbidden﴾.

His saying: ﴿and they confer together in sin and enmity and disobedience to the Messenger﴾, and this is in the sense that we explained earlier.

His saying: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you﴾. This is about the Jews. It is said that the beginning of the verse also concerns the Jews, and their greeting was that they would say: "As-samu 'alayka, O Muhammad" (death be upon you). In their language, "as-sam" meant death and destruction. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say: "And upon you." It is related in some reports that "A'ishah heard them saying that, so she began to revile and curse them, and the Prophet rebuked her for that and said to her: 'O A'ishah, indeed Allah does not love obscenity or the use of obscenity.' She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, did you not hear what they said?' The Messenger of Allah said: 'Did you not hear what I said? I said: "And upon you." Our prayer is answered concerning them, but their prayer is not answered concerning us.'"

His saying: ﴿And they say to themselves: "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ The meaning is that they used to say: "If Muhammad were a prophet, Allah would punish us for what we say."

His saying: ﴿Hell is sufficient for them﴾, that is, the torment of Hell is sufficient for them.

His saying: ﴿they will burn therein﴾, that is, they will enter it.

His saying: ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾, that is, the place of return and the final abode.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 9:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you confer privately, do not confer privately in sin and aggression and disobedience of the Messenger, but confer privately in righteousness and piety﴾. That is: and [in] that by which you guard yourselves (al-taqwa).

And His saying: ﴿And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered﴾, on the Day of Resurrection. And if we apply the verse to the hypocrites, then His saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾ means: those who believed with their tongues. The more correct view is that the address is to the believers, and Allah exalted commanded them not to be like the hypocrites and like the Jews.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Secret counsel is only from Satan﴾, meaning: that the secret counsel among them, as we have explained, is from Satan.

And His saying: ﴿so that it may grieve those who have believed﴾, i.e., that they may be grieved by what they hear of the rumour-mongering (al-irjaf) concerning the expedition (al-sariyyah).

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿but it will not harm them at all﴾, meaning: that the rumour-mongering does not harm the expedition.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿except by permission of Allah﴾, i.e., by the knowledge of Allah. And His saying: ﴿and upon Allah let the believers rely﴾, i.e., let the believers fear Allah (fa-yatawakkal being read as fa-yattaqi).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 11:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, when you are told to make room in the assemblies, then make room; Allah will make room for you﴾. Its meaning: when you are told to widen out in the assembly, that is, in the assembly of the Messenger of Allah, then widen out, and Allah will widen (His mercy) for you, that is, in Paradise.

In the exegesis (tafsir) it is related that the verse was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who was hard of hearing. He came one day when the people were seated with the Prophet, and he asked that they make room for him so that he could draw near to the Prophet and hear. They made room for him except for one man who was near the Prophet and was not made room for, and he said to him: "You have found a place, so sit down." Thabit ibn Qays rebuked him for something from his mother in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance). The Prophet heard of that and said: "O Thabit, look at the people; you have no superiority over any of them except through piety." Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, and commanded the Muslims to widen out in assemblies. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: the verse was revealed concerning the rows in jihad. The intended meaning of making room here is sitting in a place of concealment (ikhtiba'), not for war. The first view is more apparent.

As for His words: ﴿And when you are told to rise, then rise﴾, Qatadah said its meaning is: when you are called to good, then respond. Al-Hasan said: it refers to war. It has also been said: it is rising up in all matters that are good, such as jihad, the rows of congregational prayer, enjoining good and forbidding evil, and what resembles these.

In the verse there is a third view: that His words ﴿then rise﴾ refer to when the Prophet has finished, so leave from his presence and do not linger with him, lest you burden him. This is in the sense of His words: ﴿And when you have eaten, then disperse, and do not linger for conversation﴾.

As for His words: ﴿Allah will raise those of you who believe and those who have been given knowledge by degrees﴾, that is, by their faith and their knowledge. It has also been said: the Prophet used to prefer that the people of knowledge and the senior ones among his companions be near him, and others would come and draw near to the Prophet; then when the dignitaries and the people of knowledge among his companions were present, he would say: "O so-and-so, stand up, and O so-and-so, stand up and step back," so that the people of knowledge and authority might sit near him. Accordingly, the meaning of His words ﴿Allah will raise those of you who believe and those who have been given knowledge by degrees﴾ is an allusion to what the Prophet would raise them to and seat them near him. That is: they attained what they attained of elevation and rank through faith and knowledge.

As for His words: ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾, that is, All-Knowing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, precede your private consultation with a charity﴾. The occasion of revelation of the verse was that the people used to ask the Prophet excessively, and one of them would confer with the Messenger of Allah at length. So Allah wished to lighten the burden on His Prophet, and He revealed this verse. It is related from Mujahid, from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "No one acted upon this verse except me. I had a dinar, so I gave it in charity, and I consulted the Messenger privately." In another narration: he exchanged the dinar for ten dirhams, and whenever he wished to consult the Messenger, peace be upon him, privately, he would give a dirham in charity.

Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir that the hypocrites said: "The private conversation of Muhammad with his cousin has become long." The Prophet said: "I did not confer with him, but Allah conferred with him."

In some tafsirs: this (ruling) applied only for an hour of the day before it was abrogated (naskh).

Also in the tafsir: the Prophet said to ʿAli: "How much can you afford to give in charity?" He said: "A barley grain." He said: "Indeed you are frugal." And the Messenger had said: "They will give a dinar in charity." ʿAli said: "Indeed they cannot bear it."

Some of them mentioned: the hypocrites used to come to the Prophet [and confer] with him at length, out of affectation and show. So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse, and they withheld their wealth and refrained from private consultation.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is better for you and purer﴾, i.e., more pure (azka).

His saying: ﴿But if you do not find (the means), then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, i.e., if you do not find anything to give in charity, then indeed Allah has forgiven you, and has shown you mercy by dropping the charity from you.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 13:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Are you apprehensive that you will offer charity before your private consultation?﴾ mean: Are you apprehensive for your wealth, and do you withhold it?

His words: ﴿So when you do not do it, and Allah has forgiven you, then establish the prayer, give the zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ — that command was abrogated (naskh) by this verse, as if He said: "So when you do not do it, and We have abrogated it for you, then establish the prayer" — meaning: maintain it; ﴿and give the zakat⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿​﻿​﻿​​ — meaning: pay it; ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿​​﻿​​ in what they command of the matter. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do⁠﻿﻿﻿​﻿​﻿​​﻿​​﻿​​﻿​​﻿​﻿​​﻿​​﻿​﻿​​﻿​​﻿​﻿​​﻿​​﻿​​​﻿​​ — meaning: He is Knowing of your deeds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 14:

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who have taken as allies a people with whom Allah is angry?﴾ It was revealed concerning the hypocrites (munafiqun) who used to [take as allies] the Jews, and they would say to them: "We are with you in secret."

And His saying: ﴿They are neither of you nor of them﴾ means: the hypocrites.

And His saying: ﴿And they swear by a lie while they know﴾ It has been narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) called Abdullah ibn Nabtal, who was one of the hypocrites, and said to him: "Why do you insult me and harm me, and [do so with] your people and your companions?" So he left and brought his companions, who swore that they had said to him nothing but good. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And they swear by a lie while they know﴾.
And His saying: ﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾, meaning: evil were their deeds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 16:

The words of the Most High: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾ mean: they protect themselves by their oaths, just as the warrior protects himself with his shield (junnah), which is his buckler (tirs).

And His words: ﴿so they barred [others] from the way of Allah﴾ mean: they turned away from the way of Allah.

And His words: ﴿so for them there is a humiliating punishment﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

The saying of Allah, ﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah﴾, means: their wealth and their children will not ward off from them any of the punishment of Allah.

And His saying, ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾, means: they will remain forever.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day when Allah will raise them all up, and they will swear to Him just as they swear to you﴾, meaning: they will swear falsely to Allah just as they swore falsely to you.

And His saying: ﴿and they think that they are upon something﴾, meaning: they think that they are upon something.

And His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars﴾, meaning: they are the liars against Allah and against His Messenger.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 19:

His saying: ﴿Shaytan has overcome them﴾ means: Shaytan has gained mastery over them. In the descriptions of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, it is said that he was aḥwadhiyyan (adept, shrewd), unique in his kind (nasīj waḥdahu). In another narration it is aḥwaziyyan. Its meaning with the dhāl (ḥawdhī) is: dominant over affairs.

His saying: ﴿So He caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah﴾ means: Shaytan caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah.

His saying: ﴿Those are the party of Shaytan. Unquestionably, the party of Shaytan are the losers﴾ means: they have lost the good pleasure of Allah the Exalted and Paradise.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾ — we have already explained this.

And His words: ﴿those are among the most humiliated﴾ — meaning: the most lowly. Every disbeliever is humiliated, and every believer is mighty. Its meaning is: they are lowest in rank and standing.

"And His saying: ﴿God has decreed: 'I shall surely prevail, I and My messengers.'﴾ As for the victory of God, it is well known, because all things are under His will and purpose. As for the victory of His messengers, it is by aid at times and by proof at others.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, God is Strong, Mighty.﴾ That is: Strong in affairs, prevailing over them."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 58, verse 22:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾. That is: it is not a characteristic of the believers that they love those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, ﴿even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kindred﴾. Regarding the occasion of the revelation of this verse there are two opinions. The first: it was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah when he wrote to Makkah informing them of the Prophet's (ﷺ) intention to campaign against them; the story of that will come in Surat al-Mumtahanah. The second opinion: the verse was revealed concerning someone other than him.

As for His words ﴿even if they were their fathers﴾, it was revealed concerning Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, who killed his father, the disbeliever, and brought his head to the Prophet (ﷺ). It has also been said that his father died before Abu 'Ubaydah embraced Islam, and Allah knows best.

As for His words ﴿or their sons﴾, it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), who wanted to go out to his son 'Abd al-Rahman and fight him in single combat, but the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade him from that and said: "Leave him to me (to deal with)." [Note: the original phrase is "نبله مِنْهُ غَيْرك", meaning "Let someone other than you take aim at him," which is rendered here as the sense of the text.]

As for His words ﴿or their brothers﴾, it was revealed concerning 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who killed his brother Hisham ibn al-'As on the day of Badr, and he was his brother from his mother.

As for His words ﴿or their kindred﴾, it was revealed concerning Hamzah, 'Ali and 'Ubaydah ibn al-Harith (may Allah be pleased with them all), who fought against 'Utbah, Shaybah and al-Walid ibn 'Utbah, and they were their kinsmen and relatives.

As for His words ﴿those — He has written within their hearts faith﴾, that is: He has entered faith into their hearts. It has also been said: "written" means: He placed within their hearts a sign indicating their faith.

As for His words ﴿and strengthened them with a spirit from Him﴾, that is: He strengthened them with help from Him. It has also been said: with a sight from Him; and it has been said: with mercy from Him.

As for His words ﴿and will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾, its meaning is well known.

As for His words ﴿Those are the party of Allah﴾, that is: the army of Allah. It has also been said: the special ones and the elite of Allah. The Arabs say: "I am in the party of so-and-so," meaning: I am on the side and in the camp of so-and-so.

As for His words ﴿Unquestionably, the party of Allah — they are the successful﴾, that is: they are the happy ones who remain in the bliss of eternity. It has also been said: they are those who attained the pleasure of Allah the Exalted, and Allah knows best.
